messages:
Priya S: quick heads up — our pre-prod scan flagged an S3 object that contains Vault ciphertext blobs (looks like wrapped secrets). object: s3://redwood-backups/partner-ingest/2026-03-22-enc.tgz :eyes:
Alex W: can you paste the object URL or checksum? any indication of who uploaded it?
Priya S: here: https://s3.console/.../2026-03-22-enc.tgz md5: d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e. metadata shows uploader=partner-ingest-sa@partner-prod 
incident-bot: ALERT: anomalous object created in redwood-backups by partner-ingest-sa at 2026-03-22T10:12:03Z (suspected credential exposure)
Jorge M: if those are Vault-encrypted blobs the risk is if the wrapping KMS key can be used to unwrap. do we have KMS key id?
Priya S: key-id: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/wrap-kr/cryptoKeys/wrap-key-1. It’s a customer-managed HSM-backed key used for wrapping sealed secrets.
Emily (oncall): immediate containment: 1) remove partner-ingest-sa from kms:decrypt on that key, 2) create short-lived grant for partners if needed, 3) snapshot audit logs. I can run the revoke.
Alex W: agree. also enable Vault audit device if not on for that namespace and rotate wrapping key ASAP. Need a playbook so we don't break legitimate restores.
Priya S: I'm going to: 
- block kms:decrypt for partner-ingest-sa (temp)
- save current IAM policy to gs://ops/audit/policy-before.json
- snapshot Vault sealedblob index (list of paths)
- put object into quarantine bucket 'sec-quarantine'

Command I'll run now:
```
# dump current IAM
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy wrap-key-1 --location=global --keyring=wrap-kr > /tmp/policy-before.json
# remove SA decrypt
gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding wrap-key-1 --location=global --keyring=wrap-kr --member="serviceAccount:partner-ingest-sa@partner-prod" --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter"
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-backups/partner-ingest/2026-03-22-enc.tgz s3://sec-quarantine/2026-03-22-enc.tgz
```
Jorge M: +1. after revoke we should create a new key version and rewrap any legitimately needed blobs. also open cloud provider support if rotate causes problem for HSM.
Emily (oncall): FYI I'm enabling Vault audit to the splunk sink for the vault-ns that holds those sealed secrets: 
```
vault audit enable file file_path=/var/log/vault-audit.log
```
Priya S: done the IAM remove and copied object to quarantine. logs show partner-ingest-sa used to be in a role group that was recently onboarded via a partner script — I'm marking as occam candidate (likely accidental).
Alex W: we need to scope the blast radius: enumerate all sealed blobs wrapped with wrap-key-1 across buckets and repos. I'll run a scan query on the backup index.
Jorge M: for remediation plan: 
- revoke long-lived tokens that could decrypt (Vault accessor revoke sweep)
- create new wrap key version (key rotation) and schedule rewrap using controlled job (canary first)
- apply RBAC change as policy rollback for partner onboarding flow
- preserve audit trail + postmortem

Priya S: starting token sweep: `vault token revoke -accessor=<accessor>` iterating over accessors correlated to partner-sa. I'll push a short-lived token policy for partner ingest (1h TTL) after.
Emily (oncall): timeline: containment complete (10:25). next 2 hours: scan + token sweep. 24h: wrap-key rotate + rewrap job (canary then full). I'll own the canary run.
Alex W: don't forget to notify Legal for partner incident and open a ticket with PartnerOps. also export audit logs for the last 30 days for the key usage.
incident-bot: NOTE: security incident created #INC-2026-041 (severity: medium) — runbook assigned to Priya S, Emily (oncall)
Priya S: creating tracker and tagging owners. I'll also add a short checklist in the ticket: [x] quarantine object, [x] revoke SA decrypt, [ ] rotate wrap key, [ ] rewrap affected blobs, [ ] postmortem.
Jorge M: one more ask — add a KMS binding test to CI that prevents partner onboarding script from granting cryptoKeyDecrypter directly; require a review step.
Priya S: agreed — creating a patch to the onboarding pipeline now. ETA for PR: 90m.
Emily (oncall): update: canary rewrap succeeded for 50 objects, app restores validated. proceeding with scheduled rewrap in 2h.
Priya S: follow-up: partner confirmed they accidentally uploaded an export of sealed secrets from their staging. no evidence of exfil beyond the object. we'll still treat as credential exposure. postmortem tomorrow 11:00.
Alex W: thanks all. once postmortem is written, add remediation item to dev onboarding checklist.
Priya S: containment + initial cleanup done — closing this slack thread, tracking next steps in #INC-2026-041 and the postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
